content.text:
I made two small changes to `0.html`: one bug fix and one readability tweak. Neither has been tested in a browser — my headless Chrome check was blocked by the session's permissions. ## Changes **1. Fixed a rule that never applied** (`0.html:36`) The stylesheet tries to remove the top margin when one heading directly follows another (e.g. an `h2` right after the `h1`): ```css :is(h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6) + :is(h2, h3, h4, h5, h6) { margin-block-start: 0; } ``` The earlier `:is(h2, …):not(:first-child)` rule has higher specificity (0,1,1 vs 0,0,2), so it always won and stacked headings still got the 2rem gap. I wrapped the `:not()` in `:where()` to drop its specificity, so the adjacent-heading rule now takes effect: ```css :is(h2, h3, h4, h5, h6):where(:not(:first-child)) { margin-block-start: 2rem; } ``` **2. Stopped `h5`/`h6` rendering smaller than body text** (`0.html:33`) Browser defaults put them at 0.83em and 0.67em, smaller than the paragraphs they introduce. They're now `1rem`, the same size as `h4`. This one is a matter of taste, so remove the rule if you prefer the defaults. ## What I left alone The rest of the stylesheet is in good shape and I didn't find other defects.
